source: Live test on 2026-10-10: faults PR #23 (40Mi) and PR #24 (24Mi), agent PRs #25 and #26
situation: One fault on recommendationservice fired three alerts: HighMemoryUsage, then ContainerOOMKilled about 2.5 minutes later, then PodNotReady about 3 minutes after that. Dedup and the one-open-PR check keyed on the alert name, so each alert was a separate investigation, and the first two opened identical pull requests.

timeline_utc.event: HighMemoryUsage investigated; PR #25 opened, evidence score 96
ContainerOOMKilled investigated; PR #26 opened with the identical change, evidence score 98 (#25 still open)
PodNotReady investigated; evidence score 79; no PR
PR #26 closed unmerged as a duplicate

root_cause: The incident identity was the alert name. #26's proposal was valid against main (still 24Mi, #25 not yet merged) and no PR was open for its alert key, so nothing stopped it.
expected_behaviour: ContainerOOMKilled within the dedup window: same incident (namespace/service), not investigated again; a comment on the open PR with the alert and the service's current pods and events.
Its AlertManager repeats: no further comments.
PodNotReady after the PR was merged: same incident, skipped; nothing is posted (no open PR).
Any later alert after the window: investigated, but a proposal is refused while the fix was merged within SREAGENT_RECENT_MERGE_MINUTES; recorded as recently_merged.
podnotready_no_pr: Most likely the proposal was refused because main already had #25's change (merged at 17:26:35, before the PodNotReady investigation): an identical change fails the allow-list's 'does not modify anything' check. The score (79) did not stop it. Confirm from that investigation's /investigations record: pull_request.status and the propose_values_change result in tool_calls.
